boundary.value: Under the target, stored journal content and its prose derivatives will be ciphertext the operator cannot decrypt. Under the target, plaintext will exist only on the person's devices, in a vault they choose for inference, in the managed no-retention runtime while a labelled request runs there (not operator-blind while it runs), inside the enclave of a vendor-attested runtime verified under Creek-Vault ADR-0016 Decision 3 while a labelled request runs there, and at a cloud vendor under their own key sent from the device; until phase (a), BYOK is relayed through our server. Amended 2026-10-16 (#3437): with a managed vault, the writer's key and writing are relayed through our server to their vault per request, and the vault sends them to the writer's vendor, labelled on each use.

key_custody.value: User-held keys generated on the person's device; no operator escrow; the server stores ciphertext and public parameters only.

recovery.value: A recovery phrase the person writes down plus their passphrase; either unlocks the data key. Losing both means the data is gone, agreed up front at enrolment. Pairing, revocation and the rest of D03 stay open.

metadata_leakage.value: Sizes, timestamps, counts, object ids, tier labels, credit receipts and network metadata stay visible to the operator; content does not.

inference_location.value: Device first; then the person's vault-local model, a managed no-retention runtime we run, or a vendor-attested runtime verified under Creek-Vault ADR-0016 Decision 3 (all paid by credits and labelled on each use; the first two are not operator-blind while they run, and the third is held to the operator-blind target, which is not met until B24 certifies it); cloud only with the person's own key, called from the device straight to the vendor. Today BYOK is server-proxied, a known gap until phase (a).

supported_platforms.value: Web first, native later. Native apps carry the strongest guarantee; on web the guarantee rests on trusting the code we serve. Web accounts may not enrol until enforced CSP plus SRI is live; signed builds come later.

update_trust.value: Native: store-signed builds (later). Web: enforced CSP plus SRI now (live since phase (b)'s first slice), signed builds later; CSP plus SRI cannot stop us serving a different bundle.

primary_copy_removal.value: The 14 in-scope EncryptedString columns of journal_scope_proposal (of the 20; feedback and the vault credential stay out), DERIVED_FROM_PROSE plaintext, completion detection output, Creek copies, vendor copies and backups are re-encrypted client-side, withdrawn or expired before an account is labelled protected.

threat_actors.value: Defeats DB thief, backup holder, host-storage access and stored-data subpoena. Defeats the privileged operator only on native while the signed build is honest; on web the operator can capture the key through a served bundle and read all stored history until signed builds ship. A compromised device remains; inference in a managed runtime we run is not operator-blind while it runs (labelled on each use); a vendor-attested runtime verified under Creek-Vault ADR-0016 Decision 3 excludes the host and the operator from its enclave by hardware, on the vendor's attestation chain, but only while Decision 3.3 condition (f) holds, which the owner waived on 2026-10-21 and which is therefore vendor-asserted rather than verified, and the vendor keeps request metadata under condition (g); until phase (a) our server relays BYOK calls and sees their plaintext; with a managed vault it relays the key and the writing to the vault per request (amendment 2026-10-16, #3437), and neither is operator-blind while that request runs.

reopen_triggers.value: Key-non-possession prototype fails; no web anchor is buildable; D03 user testing shows unacceptable loss; B09 finds no supported non-cloud configuration.
